senses.gloss:
Snuṣā denotes the ‘daughter-in-law’ in relation primarily to her father-in-law, but also to her mother-in-law. In the latter sense the word appears in the Rigveda in the epithet su-snuṣā, ‘having a good daughter-in-law,’ used of Vṛṣākapāyī, while in the former it occurs in several passages, where the daughterin-law's respect for her father-in-law is mentioned, a respect which spirituous liquor alone causes to be violated. See also śvaśura and pati.
Foot notes x. 86, 13.
Av. viii. 6, 24; aitareya brāhmaṇa, iii. 22, 7; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, ii. 4, 6, 12.
Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, ii. 4, 2; kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xii. 12 (Indische Studien, 5, 260).
Cf. Delbrück, Die indogermanischen Verwandtschaftsnamen, 414, 415.
